issues.description: The problem UML and specification expect a Stock.emptyStock() method (emptyStock(): void), but the template Stock class provides clearInventory() instead. The solution implements emptyStock(). This name mismatch in the template vs. the specification/solution can confuse students about the required method name and cause compilation/test failures until they rename or add the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the specification: add an emptyStock() method (void) to the template Stock class (or rename clearInventory() to emptyStock()). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to reference clearInventory() if that name is preferred.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution use a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() for the same purpose. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (clearing/emptying the stock) can confuse students when mapping the diagram and requirements to the starter code and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or add a delegating emptyStock() method that calls clearInventory()) so the template matches the problem diagram and the solution implementation.
